thread:
riley: Heads-up: nightly linkcheck failed on several fragment links after the markdown pipeline update. CI shows 404s for anchors that used to work.

harper: same here. example from the job: 

bot-linkcheck: ERROR https://docs.redwood.com/guides/quickstart#installing-the-runtime -> 404 (fragment not found)

toni: I inspected one page. The headings were changed by the mdx sanitizer so the generated fragment dropped a trailing colon and also collapsed repeated hyphens. Old anchor was "installing-the-runtime:" -> new slug "installing-the-runtime". some pages lost a numeric dedupe suffix too.

riley: that's annoying because a number of examples embed the full URL with the old fragment. quick fix ideas?

harper: short-term we can have the static site serve a redirect map: data/legacy-fragments.json mapping old fragments -> new fragments. then the linkcheck will pass and real traffic will 301 to the canonical URL.

toni: I can add that file. also propose a temporary relaxed resolution flag in the linkchecker so it tries a small set of slug variants before failing: strip trailing punctuation, collapse duplicate dashes, and try with/without dedupe suffix.

riley: please make the relaxed mode opt-in and timeboxed. we don't want to hide real problems forever.

harper: agreed. I'll add a config option docs.config.linkcheck.relaxedFragmentFallback = true and default it false for now. then ops can flip it while we populate redirect mappings.

bot-linkcheck: info: rerunning job with relaxedFragmentFallback=true

devops-bot: note: different build backends behave differently: docusaurus slugify lowercases + removes punctuation; mkdocs uses a different slug rule (underscores kept). We need a canonical slug spec and a migration script to update existing headings consistently.

toni: filing a tracking issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1890 - slug spec + migration. I'll sketch the transform and a test harness that regenerates anchors for a sample set of pages.

riley: while we work on the migration, can someone grep for hard-coded fragments to prioritize fixes in snippets/examples? here's a quick ripgrep I use: 

```
rg "https?://docs\\.redwood\\.com[^\"]*#([a-z0-9_\\-:]+)" -S docs/ | sed -E 's/^.*#/#/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 50
```
harper: ran that, top hits are quickstart, runtime reference, and the tutorial series. I'll open a few tiny PRs to patch the snippets that embed full URLs.

toni: I'll land the redirect map first so the patch PRs can be smaller and safe to merge.

bot-linkcheck: linkcheck: PASS (with relaxed fallback) for commit 9b8e4d2

riley: thanks. follow-ups: 1) land redirect map (toni), 2) patch snippet embeds (harper), 3) add slug spec + test harness (toni), 4) add note to contributing docs about heading edits.

harper: I'll also add a pre-merge lint to warn when a PR changes a heading id that already exists in the versioned site. small safeguard.

devops-bot: reminder: after migration we should flip relaxedFragmentFallback=false and remove the redirect map after two weeks to keep things clean. schedule a reminder.

riley: putting a calendar reminder and adding a short blurb to the release notes about the heading normalization. :memo:

toni: will shepherd the migration issue. ping me for reviews on the redirect map and the linkcheck toggle.

bot-linkcheck: note: archived raw failures at /builds/ci/jobs/572/logs/anchor-failures.txt

riley: cool. closing the loop for now. everyone please link your PRs to #1890 so we can track progress. :white_check_mark:
